answer.reason: Nahshon's one distinct deed is that he offered first at the dedication of the altar; the other verses give only his lineage, his command, and his place in the march, which the summary already covers.

clauses.english: offered first of the princes at the dedication of the altar
clauses.quote: he that offered his offering the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab

doubts: NUM 10:14 (leading the march of Judah) was left out as a stage of a journey and covered by the summary's 'commander of Judahites'.
EXO 6:23 only names him as brother of Elisheba, and the genealogies (RUT 4, 1CH 2, MAT 1, LUK 3) only list him, so they were not cited.
